chunks: Hasan ibn Ali ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them) was asked about death: What is it? He said: My father narrated to me, from his father, from his grandfather, from al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said:
Indeed, when a believer dies, he is not dead, for the one who is truly dead is the disbeliever.
Indeed, Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, says: «He brings out the living from the dead, and He brings out the dead from the living»
That means the believer (is brought out) from the disbeliever, and the disbeliever (is brought out) from the believer.

key_terms.يُخْرِجُ الْحَيَّ مِنَ الْمَيِّتِ: He brings out the living from the dead

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the death of a believer and a disbeliever in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In *Mani al-Akhbar*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this chain from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) to redefine death as a spiritual transition rather than mere biological cessation, asserting that true 'death' belongs to the disbelievers while believers remain spiritually alive. This interpretation aligns with the Shia exegetical tradition that views the believer's soul as enduring beyond the physical body, contrasting the 'living' state of faith with the 'dead' state of disbelief. The narration emphasizes that the Quranic verse 6:95 is understood here as a metaphor for the emergence of the believer from the spiritual death of the disbeliever.
